summary_1line: Narada explains the danger of ignoring wise counsel and begins the tale of Galava, whose stubborn insistence on repaying his guru leads to an impossible demand.

image_candidates.scene_text: Viswamitra stands motionless for years with a steaming bowl of charu balanced on his head, sustaining himself only on air in his forest hermitage.
Dharma disguised as the sage Vasishtha returns after a hundred years and calmly eats the still-warm offering from the ascetic Viswamitra.
Galava, pale and emaciated with worry, laments alone while imagining the impossible task of finding eight hundred moon-white horses with one black ear.
